title: Surface area of halfspace intersections
statement: There exists a constant $C>0$ such that, for all natural numbers $n,m$ with $m\ge2$, all vectors $a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb R^n$, and all thresholds $t_1,\ldots,t_m\in\mathbb R$, the Gaussian surface area of $\{x\in\mathbb R^n: a_j\cdot x\le t_j\text{ for every }j\}$ is at most $C\sqrt{\log m}$.
hypotheses_covered: There exists a positive real constant $C$
An arbitrary list of $m$ coefficient vectors in $\mathbb R^n$
An arbitrary list of $m$ real thresholds
